paras: The killing of Henry Cole was the fatal shooting of a Black man by Deputy Sheriff Cornelius of Issaquena County at Edwards, Mississippi, on a Tuesday shortly before 4 August 1881. Cornelius had come to arrest Cole and other men accused of leaving a labor contract, and after the shooting he was jailed and bound over to the Hinds County circuit court. A Mississippi paper reported that the shooting was regarded locally as "a great outrage."

According to a special dispatch from Edwards, Cole and "some other negroes" were wanted for "violating a contract with a planter up the Mississippi river." The Chickasaw Messenger of Okolona described the men as "fugitive negroes" and said Cornelius held a warrant for their arrest.

Cornelius traveled from Issaquena County to Edwards to serve the warrant. While there, on a Tuesday, he shot and killed Cole. None of the reports describes how the encounter began, whether Cole resisted, or what became of the other men sought.

Cornelius was placed in jail, and the Okolona paper said the shooting was "regarned [regarded] as a great outrage." By 5 August the Pascagoula Democrat-Star reported that he had been bound over in the sum of $1,500 to appear before the circuit court of Hinds County. No report of an indictment, trial or verdict was found in the coverage.

Coverage was brief and appeared only in the white press. Two Mississippi papers carried the story among short state-news paragraphs: the Chickasaw Messenger on 4 August, with its note that the killing was seen as an outrage, and the Pascagoula Democrat-Star on 5 August, which mentioned only that Cornelius "shot a negro" and gave the bond. The Okolona paper gave the victim's surname only, while the Pascagoula paper did not name him at all.

Outside the South, the Edwards special ran on 4 August in a "Record of Crime" column in the Minnesota weeklies the Northern Pacific Farmer of Wadena, the Morris Tribune and the Worthington Advance. This wire version was the only one to give Cole's first name and the contract dispute behind the warrant, and it ran between unrelated crimes without comment.

reader.title: Killing of Henry Cole
bases: A deputy sheriff acting under a warrant shot and killed the man he had come to arrest; no mob or crowd is reported (A1, A2).

The Okolona item (A1) and the wire special from Edwards (A2) differ in detail (one has the jailing and 'outrage', the other the first name and the contract) and agree on the killing of Cole by Deputy Sheriff Cornelius at Edwards, and a second Mississippi paper (A5) reports the deputy bound over for the shooting.

accounts.label: Wire special from Edwards
accounts.gist: Cornelius killed Henry Cole after going to Edwards to arrest Cole and other negroes for violating a contract with a planter up the Mississippi river.

accounts.label: Mississippi state news (Pascagoula)
accounts.gist: Cornelius, who shot a negro at Edwards a few days earlier, was bound over in $1500 for the Hinds county circuit court.

framing.detail: The Okolona paper reported that the shooting was 'regarned as a great outrage' and that the deputy was in jail.
Minnesota weeklies ran the Edwards special as one line in a 'Record of Crime' column, without comment.
The Pascagoula paper gave a one-sentence note of the bond among state items, calling the victim only 'a negro'.
